task:
Write the V3 UI redesign plan (docs only): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-v3-ui-redesign-plan.md`, plus a one-line link from `docs/ROADMAP.md` "Where things stand → UI redesign" replacing the sentence that says no detailed redesign plan exists in this tree. No code changes.

OWNER DIRECTION (from the approved 1 November 2026 concept pack, which is not in the repo — summarise it faithfully from these notes, do not invent features):
- Visual: Elite Dangerous orange, glossy gunmetal, midnight navy and neon deep blue; rounded panels and buttons, soft reflections, crisp text; HUD-style condensed uppercase headings. Phase 1 (the shared design kit — tokens, Saira headings, glossy panels, opt-in pill actions, tabs, chips, pop-outs) is already implemented in PR #998 (`apps/web/src/app.css`, `design-kit.test.ts`); describe it as phase 1 done-pending-merge, and reference its tokens by name.
- Interaction model: main tasks use TABS; occasional tools use CLOSABLE, MOVABLE/DOCKABLE POP-OUTS (non-modal, focus-restoring, Escape closes — the existing Layers, Body filters and Sources & freshness pop-outs are the pattern).
- Finder: archetype selection and results first. Any = Best Colony Potential; a selected archetype = fit for that archetype. Body filters: optional grouped sliders with Reset/Cancel/Apply; applied chips stay visible when closed (shipped). 18 body counts — planets (9): Earth-like, water worlds, ammonia worlds, terraformable, gas giants, high metal content, metal-rich, rocky, icy; stars (4): black holes, neutron stars, white dwarfs, other stars; features (5): landable, walkable, rings, biological signals, geological signals. Count filters are not ranking weights; future ranking-weight dimensions are not defined and must not be invented. Controls must respect the actual API capabilities (check `apps/web/src/lib/features/explore/body-filters.ts` and the /api/local/search contract for which of the 18 exist today and list the gap honestly).
- Map workspace (review finding M09 "the map and controls do not share a useful viewport"): "Show on map" opens the selected system on demand in a map window; closing preserves search, filters, selection and scroll position; Expand enables broader exploration. The map window image defines styling and placement; implementation must embed the existing Babylon renderer with real coordinates and regions — no generated geography. The map keeps the Layers pop-out, camera controls, hover cards, Finder/catalogue split and density/nebula layers now on main.
- Inspect: Overview / Bodies / Stations tabs; seven independent economy potentials; evidence explanations in a pop-out (today: SystemRatings explanations and the Sources & freshness pop-out).
- Plan: System layout / Build order tabs, facility preview pop-out (today: the floating tabbed facility picker), explicit "Add to plan"; unknown slots remain unknown; separate Tier 2 and Tier 3 balances.
- Review/export: a pop-out over the plan; unresolved information linked to the relevant body/build; explicit DRAFT export that never claims build eligibility.
- Home: hero with primary "Explore the galaxy" and secondary "Inspect a system", three tool cards (Explore / Inspect / Plan) — largely shipped; note what remains.

WHAT THE PLAN MUST CONTAIN:
1. Phases in execution order with a one-PR-per-slice table like `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md` §7 (slice, contents, migration? visual?): phase 1 design kit (done, #998); phase 2 map workspace (M09: map window + Show on map + Expand, state preservation, tabs/pop-out structure of Explore); phase 3 Finder controls (tabs, remaining body-count groups where the API supports them, honest gaps); phase 4 Inspect tabs; phase 5 Plan tabs + review/export pop-out; phase 6 home polish and a final visual sweep. For each: files/components touched, what stays unchanged (renderer, contracts, routes, data truth), accessibility requirements (keyboard, focus, axe, reduced motion), tests (Vitest + Cypress product journey + Review Lab), and the visual-validation gate before promotion (`docs/development/v3-browser-validation-lanes.md`).
2. Non-goals and truth rules: no invented ranking weights, no generated geography, no eligibility claims, no new backend contracts without a separate design, feature-flag or incremental-merge strategy so main always ships.
3. Open owner decisions as a numbered list (e.g. default Explore layout at phone width; whether the map window is modal on mobile; which of the 18 counts to expose when the API lacks them).
Keep it concrete and under ~400 lines; link existing docs/PRs by relative path. Add a CHANGES.md entry at the top ("Docs: V3 UI redesign plan"). Run the docs contract tests that exist under `tests/` for ROADMAP/CHANGES wording (`pytest tests -k "roadmap or changes or docs" -q`) and keep them green.
